model: Sum-of-the-parts: owner-FCF DCF on Boardwalk Pipelines and Loews Hotels plus CNA stake at book-value multiple (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: 91.8% of CNA Financial at 1.0x ex-AOCI book value (equity 11,186 + AOCI deficit 1,216 at 2026-06-30 = 12,402 x 0.918)
equity_bridge.note: CNA 10-Q Q2 2026 via SEC XBRL (StockholdersEquity, AccumulatedOtherComprehensiveIncomeLossNetOfTax). Market cross-check 11,397 at CNA $45.88 on 2026-10-01. CNA's own 3,000 of senior notes are inside this book value.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Year-1 revenue growth of the modelled perimeter (Boardwalk + Hotels, FY2026E 3,270 vs FY2025 3,128, from H1 2026 run-rate: Boardwalk +3.9%, Hotels +6.9%). Consolidated CAGRs are dominated by CNA and are not the growth the engine compounds.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Consolidated equity 5yr CAGR 3.1% vs revenue 8.0% diverges >30%: FY2020 is a COVID/CNA trough base for revenue, and equity is distorted by the 2022 AOCI rate shock (equity 17,471 -> 15,201) and by 806/yr of buybacks. Per-share book compounded 9.7%/yr (BVPS ~60 at Dec-20 -> 95.3 at Dec-25). EPS 5yr CAGR is null because FY2020 EPS was -3.32.
historical_growth.notes: All consolidated series are CNA-dominated: consolidated FCF (3yr CAGR 0.6%) is insurance operating cash flow less tiny capex and is not the perimeter's owner FCF. The perimeter owner FCF (FY2025 636) has no reliable history because segment OCF is not disclosed; Boardwalk EBITDA grew 1,086 -> 1,174 (+8.1%) in FY2025 and 620 -> 639 (+3.1%) in H1 2026; Hotels pre-tax income 95 -> 52 in FY2025 (impairments, renovations) then 43 -> 106 in H1 2026 on the Epic Universe hotel ramp.

scenario_narratives.base: Boardwalk executes the $3.4B contracted backlog on schedule (Eunice-Iowa Q3 2026, Carnation and NE Texas Power Plant Q4 2027, Kosciusko Junction H1 2028), with ~$9.4B of long-term contracted revenue phasing in 2028-2030 at ~75% incremental margins; capex runs at ~32% of perimeter revenue for two years and normalises to ~14.5% by 2030. Loews Hotels completes the Epic Universe ramp (JV equity income 35 -> 85 in H1 2026 YoY) and funds Americana Arlington from operations. CNA earns ~10% on ex-AOCI book and is worth book; it keeps upstreaming ~$0.7-0.95B/yr including $2.00 specials, which the parent recycles into buybacks at a discount to this value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Texas Gateway and Petal storage expansion reach FID, extending the contracted growth runway past 2030 on LNG and data-centre gas demand; hotel segment EBITDA approaches 400 at mature Orlando occupancy; CNA's casualty rate actions outrun social inflation and its ROE recovers to 11-12% (a 1.2x mark adds ~$12/share on top of the engine's bull value, see sum_of_parts).
scenario_narratives.bear: Backlog slips a year with cost overruns and a tougher FERC rate outcome; Orlando leisure demand softens and the new hotels miss plan; at CNA, excess casualty and professional E&O reserve strengthening continues (191 of adverse development in H1 2026 alone) and the run-off long-term care block needs a top-up, so CNA is worth 0.85x ex-AOCI book (about -$8/share versus the engine's bear value, see sum_of_parts).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Loews is a holding company, so the value is the sum of what each subsidiary is worth to Loews less parent net debt, not a multiple on consolidated earnings that blend an insurer's premiums with pipeline tariffs and hotel rooms. The cash-flow businesses (Boardwalk, Hotels) are run through the house owner-FCF engine with a 10-year explicit build because the pipeline capex supercycle keeps owner FCF depressed until ~2030; the listed insurer stake is marked at ex-AOCI book because CNA's normalised ROE is about its cost of equity, and the market agrees (CNA trades at 1.0x ex-AOCI book). No conglomerate discount is applied to intrinsic value; the gap between price and value is the finding, and the 15% hurdle entry price is the margin of safety. Parent buybacks at a discount to this value are accretive to it but are not modelled as a source of value (the share count is held flat).
key_risks_to_valuation: CNA mark: every 0.1x on ex-AOCI book is ~$5.6/share (12,402 x 0.918 x 0.1 / 204.5); continued adverse casualty development or an LTC reserve charge would cut both book and the multiple

Backlog execution: the base case assumes ~$1B/yr of capex converts to ~$450-500M/yr of contracted revenue by 2030; a one-year slip costs roughly $4-5/share of PV and cost overruns are borne by Boardwalk, not customers
Hotel concentration in the Universal Orlando ecosystem; the JVs carry non-recourse debt not in net debt, so a downturn shows up as lower equity income rather than a balance-sheet hit
Interest rates: a lower rate path reduces CNA's reinvestment yield and the parent's investment income (both outside the modelled flows but inside the bridge values)
Terminal cap at 15x owner FCF binds in the base case; the valuation is ~60% terminal value and is sensitive to the midstream exit multiple
Altium Packaging carried at zero; a recovery there is upside not modelled

sum_of_parts.operating_perimeter: Boardwalk Pipelines + Loews Hotels & Co less corporate overhead; valued by the engine (see valuation.*.enterprise_value)
sum_of_parts.note: The engine holds the CNA stake at the base mark in every scenario. A full SOTP that also moves the CNA mark with the scenario would be: bear = engine bear - 8.35; bull = engine bull + 11.13; base unchanged. Those adjusted figures are in sum_of_parts.full_sotp after the build.

full_sotp.method: engine per-share value with the CNA mark moved to the scenario's P/B (bear 0.85x, base 1.0x, bull 1.2x ex-AOCI book)
full_sotp.note: Engine values 97.11 / 121.95 / 137.65 (weighted 119.67). Moving the CNA mark widens the spread but changes the weighted value by less than $1 because the bear and bull adjustments nearly offset at 25/25 weights.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 97.38-121.01. CNA price from the same endpoint on the same date.
data_sources.financials: Loews 10-K FY2025 (filed 2026-02-10, accession 0000060086-26-000008): Note 19 segment table, Boardwalk and Hotels MD&A results tables, Note 11 debt by subsidiary, Schedule I parent-only, Liquidity section. Loews 10-Q Q2 2026 (filed 2026-08-03, accession 0000060086-26-000047): six-month segment table, Boardwalk EBITDA reconciliation, Hotels results, Parent liquidity, cover share count. CNA Financial XBRL companyfacts (CIK 21175) for equity, AOCI, dividends and shares. L_Metrics.csv for consolidated history.
data_sources.qualitative: L_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): segment mix, Boardwalk backlog and in-service dates, Epic Universe hotel ramp, CNA reserve development, buyback authorisation.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 perimeter revenue = Boardwalk operating revenues and other 2,310 + Loews Hotels operating revenue 818 (10-K FY2025 Note 19 segment table; hotel reimbursable revenue 127 excluded as zero-margin pass-through; Boardwalk interest income 14 excluded). CNA is NOT in the flows -- it is valued in equity_bridge.
inputs.share_count_basis: 204,427,720 shares outstanding at 2026-07-31 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover) + 0.08M dilutive potential shares (Q2 2026 diluted table: 205.57 vs 205.50 weighted); held FLAT because the perimeter SBC is expensed in the flows. Parent buybacks (806 in FY2025, 185 in H1 2026) far exceed SBC, so the flat count is funded.
inputs.net_debt_note: Perimeter debt only (CNA's 3,000 of notes stay with CNA and are inside its book value): Parent 1,800 (500 of 4.9% 2036 notes replaced 500 of 3.8% notes in Mar-2026) + Boardwalk 3,253 (3,803 at Dec-25 less the 550 of 6.0% notes redeemed 2026-03-01; the 550 of 5.4% 2036 notes issued Nov-25 were already in the Dec-25 figure) + Loews Hotels ~1,000 (1,009 at Dec-25, mortgage loans, less amortisation). Cross-check: consolidated total debt 8,936 at 2026-06-30 (CSV) = 9,489 Dec-25 - 550 - 500 + 500 - rounding. Cash = Parent Company cash and investments net of receivables and payables, $4.4B at 2026-06-30 (10-Q Liquidity). Hotel JV debt (Universal Orlando) is non-recourse and sits inside equity income; not added.
inputs.fcf_basis_note: last_fcf is the FY2025 owner FCF of the MODELLED PERIMETER (Boardwalk + Hotels - corporate overhead), built from the segment note: EBITDA 1,337 (Boardwalk 1,174 less 14 interest income; Hotels pre-tax 52 + interest 69 + D&A 100 + impairment 25 = 246; less corporate admin 69) - SBC 16 - D&A 545 = EBIT 776 x (1-24%) = 590 + D&A 545 - capex 499 (Boardwalk 354 + Hotels 143 + corporate 2) = 636. reported_fcf 2,700 is the CONSOLIDATED CSV figure (OCF 3,279 - capex 579) and includes CNA's insurance operating cash flow, which this model values through the bridge at book, not through the flows -- the two are not meant to reconcile by subtraction.
inputs.sbc_source: Estimate. Consolidated SBC add-back is $41M (10-K FY2025 cash flow statement) and is predominantly CNA; the non-insurance perimeter is not separately disclosed and is charged at 0.5% of perimeter revenue (~$16M). Equity-award taxes not separately disclosed; immaterial at this scale.
inputs.interest_income_note: Corporate segment net investment income FY2025 (196; 242 in FY2024; 50 in H1 2026) is the return on the Parent Company cash and investment pile. Stripped from the flows because that pile is added back in net debt (matching-asset rule). Boardwalk's own 14 of interest income is likewise stripped from its EBITDA. CNA's net investment income stays inside CNA's earnings and book value, which are valued in the bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 treasury purchases 806 (8.9M shares); H1 2026 185 (1.7M shares, 1.4M of them in Q2 for 148). Cumulative authorisation raised to $80B in May 2026 is a limit, not a commitment.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 7.5% blended for a BBB-rated contracted interstate gas pipeline (Boardwalk, ~80% of perimeter EBITDA) and an owned/JV hotel operator (~20%). USD build: 10y UST ~4.2%, ERP 5%, pipeline beta ~0.9 gives cost of equity ~8.7%; Boardwalk pre-tax cost of debt ~5.4% (Nov-2025 5.4% notes), after-tax ~4.1%; ~40% debt weight -> ~6.9% for the pipeline; hotels at ~9.5% lifts the blend to 7.5%. Same WACC in every scenario (risk charged once, through the weights).
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial to the perimeter (pipeline rights-of-way and hotel ground leases are in operating costs); no separate lease charge and no lease liabilities in net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: The only material NCI is the 8.2% of CNA not owned by Loews. It is handled by valuing only Loews' 91.8% share of CNA book in the bridge; CNA is not in the flows, so there is no NCI deduction elsewhere. Hotel minority interests were bought out in 2025 (41).
inputs.cna_ownership_note: 91.8% derived from the NCI share of CNA net income (105 of 1,278 in FY2025; 44 of 532 in H1 2026). CNA shares outstanding 270.6M at 2026-07-30 (CNA 10-Q cover).
inputs.altium_note: The ~53% equity-method stake in Altium Packaging (equity-method loss 28 in each of FY2024 and FY2025; 'substantial indebtedness') is excluded from BOTH the flows and the bridge -- the loss is stripped and the asset is carried at zero. Conservative; its carrying value is not disclosed in the segment note.
inputs.notes: MODEL: sum-of-the-parts, because Loews straddles two routing rows -- a ~92%-owned listed commercial P&C insurer (CNA, ~81% of consolidated revenue, meaningless to an FCF engine) and two cash-flow operating businesses (Boardwalk Pipelines, wholly-owned interstate gas pipelines in a $3.4B contracted growth-capex cycle; Loews Hotels & Co, owned hotels plus 50% Universal Orlando JVs). Per SKILL.md the parts are valued separately and summed: (1) the engine runs an owner-FCF DCF on the Boardwalk + Hotels perimeter net of corporate overhead, 10-year horizon because the pipeline capex supercycle (capex 32% of revenue in 2026-27 falling to ~14% by 2030) keeps owner-FCF margin ramping until ~2030; (2) Parent + Boardwalk + Hotels debt less the Parent cash/investment pile is the net debt; (3) Loews' 91.8% of CNA is added in equity_bridge at 1.0x ex-AOCI book (CNA equity 11,186 + AOCI deficit 1,216 = 12,402 at 2026-06-30; x 0.918 = 11,385). The 1.0x mark follows from CNA's normalised ROE ex-AOCI of ~10% (FY2025 1,278 on ~12.3B; H1 2026 annualised ~8.6% after 191 of adverse casualty development and 148 of cat losses) against a ~10% cost of equity, and it equals CNA's market value to Loews on the valuation date (270.6M x $45.88 x 0.918 = 11,397). The bridge is top-level in this engine so CNA sits at the same mark in all three scenarios; the scenario spread in the engine is the operating businesses only, and the bear weight is lifted to 25% as the proxy for CNA underwriting/reserve risk. The sum_of_parts block shows the per-share effect of moving the CNA mark to 0.85x (bear) and 1.2x (bull). Price is a regular close, not after-hours. No holdco discount is applied to intrinsic value -- the discount is what the market applies, and the 15% hurdle entry price is the margin of safety.

bear.narrative: FERC certificate delays and steel/labour cost overruns push the backlog's in-service dates out a year and its cost up (capex stays elevated while revenue arrives late); an adverse FERC rate case trims re-contracting rates; a consumer downturn hits Orlando theme-park attendance so the new hotels never reach plan. Exit multiple capped at 13x.

base.growth_note: 2026E +4.5% from H1 run-rate; 2027 Eunice-Iowa full year; 2028-29 Carnation + NE Texas Power Plant (Q4 2027) and Kosciusko Junction (H1 2028) in service -- the $3.4B backlog carries ~$9.4B of contracted revenue, ~$450-500M/yr once fully in service, phased 2028-2030; then FERC-contracted escalation ~2.5%.
base.margin_note: Perimeter EBITDA after corporate admin (69). FY2025 actual 42.7% was depressed by low-margin ethane product sales (+137 revenue at ~nil margin) and hotel JV impairments; H1 2026 ran 48% (seasonally strong). 2026E: Boardwalk ~1,220 (50.8%) + Hotels ~330 (38%) - overhead 65 on 3,270. Incremental contracted transport revenue carries ~75% margins, lifting the blend to 49% by 2030.
base.da_note: FY2025 545/3,128 = 17.4%; rises as the $3.4B of new pipe is placed in service, then eases as revenue catches up.
base.capex_note: 2026 guided: Boardwalk ~845 (225 maintenance + 620 growth) + Hotels ~190 (incl. start of the ~$400M Americana Arlington project, opening 2029) = ~1,037 = 31.7%. Backlog spend peaks 2027, tapers through 2029-30; terminal 14.5% = maintenance (~325) plus modest ongoing growth, set a little below D&A because pipeline D&A on a $12B gross base structurally exceeds maintenance (FY2025: 443 vs 194).
base.tax_note: Boardwalk FY2025 effective 24% (140/584); near-term cash rate below that on 100% bonus depreciation for the growth capex, ramping back to 24%.
base.cap_note: 15x owner FCF (~10-11x EBITDA) is where contracted midstream trades; Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% would imply 20.5x and the cap binds.

bull.narrative: Texas Gateway (Katy/Carthage to Gillis) reaches FID off the 2026 open season and Petal storage expands, adding a second wave of contracted LNG-feedgas and power-generation capacity on top of the $3.4B backlog (hence higher 2027-29 capex and 11-12% growth); the three Epic Universe hotels run at mature occupancy and rate, pushing hotel EBITDA toward 400 and the perimeter margin to 52%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% default to 25% because roughly 45% of the sum-of-the-parts is the CNA stake, which sits at one fixed mark in the engine's bridge: the extra bear weight is the proxy for the social-inflation reserve risk, the long-term-care run-off tail and rate sensitivity that the operating-only scenarios cannot express. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because the bull case needs several independent things to go right -- Texas Gateway FID, a mature Orlando ramp and a CNA re-rating. Base 50%: the backlog is contracted and FERC-approved in large part, and the hotel ramp is already visible in H1 2026.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position is not meaningful here: the house/street gap is ~$1.9/share (perimeter SBC 0.5% of revenue) and the price sits ~$15 below both, so the ratio is a large negative. Read house and street as coincident; the valuation does not depend on SBC treatment.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
